title: Affine characteristic-p constant cohomology vanishes above degree one
statement: Let $X$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], $p$ a prime, and suppose $p\cdot1=0$ in $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. For every integer $q\geq2$, $H^q(X_{\mathrm{et}},\underline{\mathbf Z/p\mathbf Z})=0$, with cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] and constant sheaf [def-sc-constant-sheaves]. This includes the empty scheme.

source.place: Lemma lemma-vanishing-affine-char-p-p, part (1), and its proof from the Artin-Schreier sequence and affine structure-sheaf acyclicity.

proof.text: For $G$ the lifted associated structure-module sheaf, take the short exact complex $S=(\underline{\mathbf F_p}\to G\to G)$ from [lem-sc-artin-schreier-sequence-scheme].

Write $q=(n+1)+1$ with $n\geq0$. The structure module is quasi-coherent, so [lem-sc-etale-affine-qcoherent] gives $H^{n+1}(X,G)=0$ and $H^{n+2}(X,G)=0$. The latter vanishing makes the connecting map $H^{n+1}(X,G)\to H^{n+2}(X,\underline{\mathbf F_p})$ surjective by the long exact Ext cohomology sequence [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-ext-cohomology-long-exact], concretely the proved source lemma Sheaf.H.δSucc_surjective. Its source is a subsingleton by the former vanishing, so its target is a subsingleton. Arithmetic identifies this degree with $q$. This is exactly the compiled Lean proof, using Function.Surjective.subsingleton. The boundary case q=2 uses H¹(G)=H²(G)=0, not H⁰(G)=0.
